title: Cap. IX Resp.: God confers corporal and spiritual benefits on the reprobate — therefore not strict right; false dichotomy with highest mercy
pass_a_gloss: But he confers upon them from time to time many benefits both corporal and spiritual by which they may be made better, and he subtracts nothing that is owed them, nor does he pour into them anything whereby they may be made worse. Therefore he does not deal with them by strict right. But the adversaries so plead this cause as if between these two, to deal from highest mercy, and to deal from highest or strict right, there were no middle.
pass_b_english: But he often confers on them many corporal and spiritual benefits by which they may be made better; he withdraws nothing owed them, and pours into them nothing by which they are made worse. So he does not deal with them by strict right. Yet the adversaries plead as if between dealing from highest mercy and dealing from highest or strict right there were no middle.
source_text: At confert in eos subinde multa tum corporalia, tum spiritualia beneficia quibus reddantur meliores, et nihil quod illis debitum est subtrahit, nec illis infundit quicquam quo reddantur deteriores. Non igitur stricto jure agit cum illis. Sed adversarii ita hanc causam agunt, quasi inter haec duo, agere ex summa misericordia, et agere ex summo vel stricto jure, nihil esset medium.
